editorial:
You follow two young guys who stumble into a huge Pentagon arms deal. David Packouz and Efraim Diveroli turn small-time gun sales into a massive contract to arm America's allies in Afghanistan. It is wild, funny, and tense, showing how greed and ambition can pull ordinary people into a dangerous world. The tone mixes buddy comedy with crime drama, with lots of fast deals, travel, and bad decisions that keep you watching.

Miles Teller and Jonah Hill carry the movie with strong chemistry, making you laugh even when things get risky. The pacing moves quickly, though some middle parts feel repetitive. Pros include sharp humor, true-story shock, and an energetic soundtrack. Cons include characters who can be unlikable and moral lessons that stay light. Watch it if you like crime comedies and real-life scandals. Stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, David and Efraim's partnership collapses after a dangerous deal goes wrong and government investigators close in on them. Efraim is arrested and sent to prison, while David avoids jail but loses the money and friendship. The twist is that their huge success was built on risky shortcuts, so the ending shows ambition turning into betrayal and consequences.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves crime comedies, true stories, and buddy movies.
